title: Mount a full malt cup on a spindle drink mixer so the motor runs
instruction: Mix the milkshake: put the filled steel cup on the drink mixer with the spindle inside it, its base on the upper step of the cup rest and its rim in the cup guide, so the mixer runs. Do not spill the mix.
context: Ice cream shops, diners and burger counters blend milkshakes on spindle drink mixers that have no button: the full steel cup is tipped so its mouth takes in the hanging agitator, lifted around the spindle with its rim going up behind the cup guide, and set on the cup rest. On the rest's upper step the rim holds the guide's switch pin up and the motor runs; the lower step only holds the cup. Tipped too far, the mix spills. Daily work for counter staff (O*NET 35-3023.00: "Prepare and serve cold drinks, frozen milk drinks, or desserts, using drink-dispensing, milkshake, or frozen custard machines.").
setup: Metres; station counter (stainless steel top) z=0.7475, x -0.19 to 0.91, y -0.65 to 0.65; x forward, y left, z up; arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75). Drink mixer, fixed by its suction feet: single-spindle commercial drink mixer (Hamilton Beach HMD200 size, 20.5 x 6.5 x 6.75 in, 6.4 kg), die-cast metal housing. Mixer frame: origin (0.277,-0.145,0.7475) on the counter under the spindle, turned 30 degrees about z so +x points straight away from the right arm's base (0.32 m from it), toward the column; millimetres in that frame below. Base 25 tall, 165 wide, x -60 to 111 with a rounded front. Column x 60 to 111, 96 wide at its face, up to the head. Head z 375 to 521, 165 wide, x -75 to 111. Spindle, stainless steel, free to spin: 8 mm shaft hanging from the head on x=y=0 to a solid 27 mm agitator disc 6 thick at z 208 to 214; 20 mm chuck at z 340 to 375. Cup rest, chrome-plated steel J bracket on the column face, 18 wide: run step x 26 to 56 with its top at z 160, standby step x 12 to 26 with its top at z 152, back plate x 56 to 60 up to z 178, all from z 130. Cup guide, chrome-plated steel plate 3 thick hanging from the head, z 326 to 375, inside the mouth of a seated cup: back face at x 45.9 for |y| up to 6, 44.7 for 6 to 12, 42.7 for 12 to 18. Switch pin, white plastic, 9 x 8 x 20 tall at x 47 to 56, lower end at z 336.6 at rest, slides up 0 to 12 mm on a 120 N/m spring preloaded 1.2 N, 4 g; the motor switch closes at 2 mm of lift. Malt cup: 32 oz stainless steel drink-mixer cup (110E size), 180.6 tall, 96.5 across the top under a rolled lip 102.4 across, 70 across the base, wall modelled 1 mm (outside true); filled with the maker's recipe (3 No. 24 scoops of ice cream, 4 fl oz milk, 1.5 fl oz syrup: 281 ml), 0.58 kg in all, centre of mass 64 mm above its bottom. It stands upright on the counter, bottom centre at world (0.301,-0.479,0.7475) (0.347 m from the right arm's base, 30 degrees to its right), turned -30 degrees about z. Friction static/dynamic 0.30/0.25 for the cup and the mixer (estimates). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: From the cup's pose and velocity, the switch pin's lift and the gripper positions at 20 Hz; the score is the value at the end. Mixer frame as in the setup (mm). Seated on the run step: the cup's bottom centre 2 below to 3 above z 160, its bottom's back edge at least 2 past the step's front edge (x 26), axis within 5 degrees of vertical, bottom centre within 10 of y=0, the rim's inner top edge on the column side at least 3 above the guide plate's lower edge (z 326), no more than 1.5 in front of the plate's back face and within |y| 18, and the pin lifted at least 2 (motor on). Seated on the standby step: the same at z 152 (front edge x 12) with the pin lifted under 2 (motor off). Spindle in: the agitator's centre inside the cup at least 40 below the lip and above the mix layer, 2 clear of the wall, with the cup's bottom at least 30 above the counter. Released: both gripper TCPs at least 30 from the cup's bounding box. Still: under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s. Zero for the rest of the run: the cup tips more than 65 degrees from upright (the recipe's surface reaches the lip at about 69), or its bottom centre goes more than 20 below the counter top or off the counter. Score: 1.0 seated on the run step, released and still for 1 s; 0.5 seated on the run step otherwise, or seated on the standby step released and still for 1 s; 0.25 seated on the standby step otherwise, or spindle in; 0 otherwise. Real trial: the motor running, and a side photo against a scale for the step and the tilt.
reset_notes: Lift the cup off the rest and out of the guide, tip it clear of the spindle and stand it on its mark, turned the same way; the switch pin drops back. Nothing is consumed in simulation. Real trials: refill to the recipe (or a 0.3 kg thick stand-in) and wipe the spindle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The mix is a rigid layer on the cup's bottom giving the full cup its 0.58 kg and centre of mass; it does not slosh, and spilling is scored from the cup's tilt (65 degrees; liquid reaches the lip at 69). The motor is not simulated: it runs when the pin is lifted 2 mm. Cup wall 1 mm (0.6 real). The cup rest, guide, pin, agitator and the cup's base and mass are scaled from the maker's photos or estimated; friction is estimated.
